About Gusto
At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.
All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .
AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

This is your chance to shape the foundation of a fast-growing, high-impact part of Gusto's business as a Senior Sales Operations Analyst supporting our Health Insurance (HI) Sales team. You'll build the insights and AI-powered solutions that make a large, high-volume sales organization, supporting 80+ reps across two segments.

You'll sit at the intersection of data, process, and execution; you'll turn real sales challenges into the tools, reports, automations, and workflows that move the numbers.
You'll help grow a business segment that serves tens of thousands of small businesses through smarter, data-driven sales strategies. If you thrive where analytics, problem-solving, and supporting others meet, this role offers ownership, visibility, and the chance to influence how Gusto sells health insurance.

The HI Sales Operations team partners closely with sales leadership to support two dynamic, fast-moving sales teams that contribute meaningfully to Gusto's growth. We think of ourselves as builders, problem solvers, and strategic partners; we turn uncertainty into clarity and fragmented processes into scalable, repeatable systems.
Our work spans quotas, pipeline health, forecasting, process design, data integrity, account and territory administration, go-to-market strategy, and increasingly, AI-driven optimization. We value curiosity, open communication, and a commitment to helping 80+ sales reps operate efficiently and confidently.

Analytics, Reporting & Forecasting
Build, automate, and maintain reports and dashboards that track sales performance, funnel metrics, pipeline health, SLAs, and rep productivity; keep definitions consistent and documentation clear.
Partner with RevOps, Finance, Marketing, and Analytics to produce operational reporting, revenue insights, and forecasting models across the weekly forecast, monthly reviews, and QBR cadence.
Own metric definitions and data accuracy so leaders trust the numbers they act on.
Drive AI Strategy for Sales
Identify and prototype AI and automation tools, such as content generation, analytics copilots, and call coaching, that remove manual friction from the sales process.
Partner with Sales, BizTech, Product, and Enablement to embed AI into daily sales workflows, improving both efficiency and effectiveness.
Source and lead net-new AI and automation projects, connecting data insights to process improvements that lift rep productivity.
Process Design & Continuous Improvement
Examine workflows and rep performance to identify bottlenecks; recommend and implement process and automation changes that improve conversion, efficiency, and the rep experience.
Partner with Sales Enablement to document processes, build playbooks, and drive adoption of new tools and workflows.
Operational Support & Problem-Solving
Provide day-to-day support to HI Sales leadership and reps: ad hoc data requests, process issues, and one-off investigations.
Own account and territory administration as the business evolves, assignment and coverage upkeep, book reassignments for leave and departures, large-scale account rerouting, and segment reclassification, supported by lead-routing and round-robin automation.
Support territory, quota, and coverage planning, plus monthly sales-compensation reconciliation.
Troubleshoot reporting issues, broken workflows, missing CRM data, and gaps in pipeline visibility with fast, accurate fixes.
Cross-Functional Partnership & Communication
Work closely with Sales Leadership, RevOps, Finance, BizTech, and Product to keep everyone aligned and remove obstacles to progress.
Translate sales challenges into clear business requirements; partner cross-functionally to design solutions and durable improvements.
Keep stakeholders aligned with clear, regular updates to managers and senior leadership on timelines, risks, and outcomes.
Act as a trusted advisor, bringing structure, insight, and clarity to complex or ambiguous problems.

5+ years in Sales Ops, RevOps, or a similar analytical GTM role; ideally in a fast-paced SaaS or fintech environment.
Strong Salesforce proficiency; you can spot data issues, audit pipeline problems, manage account ownership and routing, and build reports and dashboards that reps and leaders actually use.
Analytical depth across Salesforce reports and dashboards, SQL, Tableau or Looker, and Excel/Google Sheets.
Hands-on experience with forecasting, pipeline management, and territory or quota planning on a recurring cadence; for example, a weekly forecast feeding monthly reviews and QBRs.
Comfort evaluating AI and automation tools and prototyping simple workflows to improve productivity.
Excellent written and verbal communication; you simplify complex information and create alignment from frontline reps to senior directors.
A first-principles problem solver who breaks down ambiguous issues, tests hypotheses, and builds structured solutions.
Exceptionally organized and detail-oriented, you manage multiple projects and recurring workflows while protecting data quality and operational reliability.
A strong partner to sales, with a track record supporting teams that have competing, fast-changing priorities.

Experience in payroll, HR tech, or SMB SaaS go-to-market motions.
Experience supporting a regulated or compliance-driven sales segment such as health insurance or benefits.
Experience designing or implementing automations, AI workflows, or similar tooling.
A track record of building cross-functional relationships across Sales, BizTech, and Analytics.
Experience building systems to support new or evolving sales motions, with comfort in fast iteration and testing in live sales environments.

Storyblok is hiring a Deal Operations Manager to build the operating workflow for how deals are structured, reviewed, approved, executed, and handed off across quote-to-cash.

The role supports Sales on deal construction and deal design strategy, coordinates Legal execution, partners with Finance on revenue recognition readiness, and turns pricing, packaging, and NPI decisions into field-ready operating process.

Sitting within Revenue Operations, this role works across Sales, Sales Leadership, Finance, Legal, Deal Strategy, Systems, Order Management, Security, Customer Success, and Product / Packaging to make approval-ready deals faster and downstream defects lower.

Deal operations workflow and process
Build the global deal operations workflow for intake, routing, approval readiness, SLAs, escalation paths, and exception handling.
Own approval readiness in DealHub CPQ, including required fields, quote quality checks, approval context, discount rationale, and downstream handoff inputs.
Maintain practical process documentation, templates, and decision rules so Sales can move standard deals through documented paths.
Deal construction and design strategy support
Support Sales and Sales Leadership on deal construction across new business, renewal, expansion, multi-year, ramped, multi-product, and non-standard commercial requests.
Translate deal strategy into approval-ready constructs with clear value exchange, risk flags, concession logic, billing terms, contract timing, and implementation assumptions.
Partner with Deal Strategy, Customer Success, Product / Packaging, and Finance when commercial design affects retention, expansion, product adoption, or reporting.
Legal execution and Finance revenue recognition readiness
Engage Legal early on non-standard terms, contract language, execution path, risk ownership, and customer-requested changes.
Coordinate with Finance on revenue recognition inputs, billing terms, payment terms, start dates, product lines, order form clarity, and required approval evidence.
Maintain pre-signature checks for deals with rev rec, billing, custom terms, or product readiness risk.
Pricing, packaging, NPI, and DealHub CPQ rollout
Participate in pricing and packaging execution and strategy support so decisions can be turned into field process, DealHub CPQ logic, approval paths, and reporting readiness.
Support NPI rollout by defining deal rules, quote requirements, launch constraints, fallback paths, and field guidance for early transactions.
Track whether pricing, packaging, or NPI changes create quote exceptions, approval confusion, billing defects, or customer handoff issues.
Quote-to-cash quality, cadence, and continuous improvement
Own the operating handoff from approved quote to order, billing, commissions, reporting, and customer lifecycle records.
Run the deal operations cadence with KPI packs, defect logs, root-cause reviews, action owners, and process improvements.
Identify automation and AI use cases tied to intake, routing, approval summaries, quote checks, documentation, and measurable cycle-time reduction.

Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years in Deal Desk, Deal Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or a comparable commercial operations role, ideally in B2B SaaS.
Hands-on experience with CPQ tooling (DealHub or comparable) and quote-to-cash / lead-to-cash processes.
Demonstrated experience structuring and reviewing non-standard deals (multi-year, ramped, expansion, multi-product) and partnering with Sales on deal construction.
Working knowledge of revenue recognition concepts, billing and order processes, and coordinating contract execution with Legal and Finance.

Grove Collaborative is a sustainability-focused consumer products company creating household and personal care essentials that are effective, beautifully designed, and healthier for people and the planet. We are a certified B Corp, plastic-neutral, and on a mission to transform the CPG industry for good.
Merchandising Operations Manager
Grove's merchandising operation is full of good instincts running on manual work. This role exists to fix that: redesign the core processes, then personally build the automation that makes them stick. This is a rare shot at rebuilding how merchandising actually runs, and at proving AI belongs in the hands of the person closest to the problem, not just the AI team.
We're not hiring someone to write a strategy memo about AI and hand it off. We're hiring someone who will map the workflow, feel where it breaks, and then sit down and build the thing that fixes it.
More About the Opportunity
Merchandising at Grove runs on real expertise and too much manual glue.
Buyers chase vendors for the same data, week after week.
Marketing launches promotions inventory finds out about too late.
Good people spend their time on work a workflow should be doing for them.
We have an internal AI team. They coach. They don't build for you.
This role is for the person who wants their hands on the keyboard, not the person who scopes it and waits.
The honest version: no template here. You're defining the standard as you go, with review at key milestones and real autonomy in between.
Some of what you build will work on the first try. Some won't. That's the job.
What You'll Own
Map how merchandising actually works today, not how the org chart says it works.
Redesign core operating processes for speed, accuracy, and margin protection: assortment planning, item setup, pricing and markdown, vendor and PO management, allocation, replenishment.
Own the calendar connecting marketing activations to inventory, so launches are stock-backed, not a surprise to the warehouse.
Translate activation plans into buy, allocation, and replenishment signals; flag stock risk before launch, not after.
Coordinate vendor commitments tied to activations: fill rates, lead times, launch quantities.
Build self-service tools and proactive alerts that scale the buyer-vendor relationship, including visibility into vendor performance.
Build the automation yourself, using Claude and comparable AI tools, no/low-code platforms, and lightweight automation, from concept through rollout.
Run pilots end to end: scope, build, test for accuracy, validate fit, scale. Keep humans in the loop on margin- and inventory-critical decisions.
Maintain a registry of approved tools and active automations, so what exists and what it's for is never a mystery.
Own change management for every rollout: training, AI literacy for non-technical audiences, office hours, a bench of power users.
Build reporting on process and automation performance, and use it to prioritize what gets built next.

Real fluency in retail merchandising operations, not an adjacent function you've watched from a distance.
You've mapped a broken process and redesigned it, not just diagnosed it.
Basic technical acumen and a genuine willingness to build, no engineering background required.
Comfortable working with a specialist team as a coaching resource, not a build team, and taking their guidance without handing off your job.
You've run a pilot from scoping through adoption, and you know the gap between a demo and something people actually use.
You care about the boring, durable stuff: documentation, SOPs, registries, training, the things that outlast the person who built them.
You think in workflows and root causes, not tickets.
You know the difference between a problem worth automating and one worth leaving alone.
Even Better if You Have
Built something with Claude or a comparable AI tool that a non-technical team now relies on.
Experience connecting marketing or demand planning to inventory and allocation.
Designed a self-service tool that measurably cut manual buyer-vendor back-and-forth.
A retail, CPG, or commerce background with real fluency in vendor and marketplace dynamics.

Execute daily trust and custody computations by the strict deadline of 12:00 PM SGT in compliance with Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations (SF(LCB)R).

Monitor Financial Resources to ensure continuous compliance above Total Risk Requirement (TRR) limits. Partner closely with Corporate Accounting, Treasury, RHS Clearing, and Engineering teams to support system transitions (e.g., system migrations, report automation) and cross-train across broader global entity reporting.

Deep understanding of MAS Risk-Based Capital (RBC) frameworks, SF(LCB)R requirements, and capital requirements for broker-dealers in Singapore.
5+ years of experience in financial operations or regulatory reporting within a broker-dealer or financial institution in Singapore.
Experience managing back-office ledger systems, Swift/API data feeds, and reporting automation using tools like Excel/Google Sheets (SQL or data visualization tools like Superset are a plus).
Strong self-starter attitude with proven success operating independently in a fast-paced environment and managing time-sensitive regulatory deadlines (e.g., 12:00 PM SGT daily deliverables).
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills to partner with global teams across varying time zones.

Role Overview Maneva is seeking a People & Business Operations Manager to build and lead our people operations function at a critical stage of growth.

This role sits at the intersection of employee lifecycle management, governance, business operations, and culture.

You'll own performance management infrastructure, compensation and benefits administration, employee relations, U.S. state-level employment compliance as we expand our U.S. footprint, and will help drive the initiatives of the strategy and business operations team.

You'll be responsible for building the systems that let us hire, develop, and retain great people as we continue our fast expansion. You'll work closely with the Talent Manager, Finance, Business Operations, and the broader executive leadership team, and act as a trusted advisor to the CEO and leadership team on people matters.

Key Responsibilities U.S. Employment Compliance Own state-by-state compliance as Maneva expands its U.S. employee base: tax registration, payroll setup, mandatory workplace posters, and required employee notices, all of which vary by state.

Build and maintain a repeatable process for evaluating new-state requirements as hiring expands, rather than handling each state reactively. Partner with Rippling, outside counsel, and Finance to ensure payroll, tax, and notice obligations are met on schedule for every state in which Maneva has employees.

Serve as Maneva 's go-to internal expert on U.S. state employment law as it applies to a distributed, remote-first workforce. Performance Management & Levelling Design and execute performance review cycles (6-month and annual) across the organization, tailored to company growth stage and business needs.

Own and maintain levelling frameworks across engineering (IC1–IC6) and non-technical roles; define competencies, expectations, and progression criteria, building on the framework already in place. Partner with department heads and the Talent Manager to calibrate performance data and inform talent decisions.

Design and facilitate manager training on feedback, goal-setting, and performance conversations. Maintain performance documentation and analytics to inform strategic people decisions. Compensation Administration Own day-to-day execution of compensation administration across all job levels and geographies; maintain salary bands.

Execute variable/commission plans for sales and other roles; ensure alignment with business goals. Execute ROE submissions, payroll adjustments, and comp/commission payouts, routing every payout through Finance for cost sign-off. Handle market increases, retention bonuses, and compensation requests with appropriate approvals.

Benefits & Wellness Administration Own benefits administration across the US and Canada. Coordinate benefits enrollment, education, and communication; manage plan changes. Administer COBRA coverage, health plan compliance, and employee welfare programs. Track and optimize benefits costs; provide leadership with regular reporting.

Own employee handbook and policy management for both Canada and the U.S.; refresh as laws and entities change. Manage people-related compliance: ROE submissions, payroll tax filings, and employment law compliance across all jurisdictions.

Maintain data integrity across HRIS systems; ensure clean records for auditing. Coordinate with external employment counsel as needed. Culture & Employee Engagement Partner with the Talent Manager on culture initiatives and engagement programs. Own recognition programs, including birthday and work-anniversary recognition.

Monitor and report on employee engagement signals; identify retention risks. Facilitate communication between leadership and employees. Systems, Automation & Operations Build automated workflows. Create dashboards and reporting for leadership on key HR metrics. Manage systems integration; ensure clean data flow between platforms.

Take ownership of ad-hoc projects and strategic initiatives. Assist with insurance requirements and vendor/partnership coordination as needed.

Support with ad-hoc strategic initiatives such as fundraising and data room management, and partnership outreach. Support KPI and revenue schedule tracking in coordination with Finance Expect this allocation to flex up (e.g., during fundraising) and back down as business needs shift.

Passion for building cultures where people feel valued and connected to mission. Technical Skills & Tools Proficiency with HRIS systems (Rippling preferred). Comfort building automation tools. Strong Excel and analytics skills. Nice to Have Experience in B2B SaaS, deep tech, or AI/manufacturing.

· Strengthen documentation so processes are durable, repeatable, and not person dependent.

· Use AI to automate manual, repetitive workflows, chaining multiple steps to move from raw data to finished output and measurably reduce the time your work takes.

· Share what you build so teammates can replicate it, raising the whole team's efficiency, not just your own.

· Spot the most manual, repetitive, and high volume work in your domain and prioritize it for automation, going after the biggest reductions in effort first.

As the Regional General Manager, you will provide strategic leadership and direction to deliver safe operations while driving excellence in operational performance and guest service through our contracted service partners across the designated region.

Reporting directly to the Vice President of Airports, you will lead a team of Regional Managers and collaborate closely with internal and external stakeholders to maintain regulatory compliance, foster positive relationships, and ensure a consistent, high-quality guest experience across all airport touchpoints within the region.
This role requires an experienced leader who holds service partners accountable for delivering WestJet's operational and service standards while balancing the needs of our guests, our partners, and our business. You will coach and support service partners in developing and executing airport action plans that address performance gaps, strengthen safety, and improve the guest experience.
The Regional General Manager will provide strategic oversight of airport operations across the region by identifying emerging risks, monitoring operational performance, and ensuring consistent execution of WestJet's standards and priorities. Foster a Safety Above All culture with Regional Managers by ensuring service partners achieve safety targets, monitoring performance trends, and addressing operational risks.

Provide strategic oversight of airport operations, ensuring consistent execution of WestJet's operational and guest standards and priorities.
Deliver regional operational performance by achieving operational, guest experience, and financial objectives while driving continuous improvement through station action plans.
Provide governance through audits, operational reviews, and performance assessments to ensure adherence to standards, identify risks, and drive corrective actions.

Build and maintain executive relationships with airport authorities, service partner leadership, government agencies, bargaining agents, and other key stakeholders.

OR EDUCATION: You may substitute education for specialized experience as follows: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M., if related. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: You may qualify on a combination of education and experience.

To combine education and experience, the total percentage of experience at the required grade level compared to the requirement, as well as the percentage of completed education compared to the requirement must equal at least 100 percent.

Only graduate level education in excess of the first 36 semester hours (54 quarter hours) may be combined to be considered for qualifying education. For the GS-09, you must have one year of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service.

Specialized Experience for this position includes: Assisting others in performing analytical duties in support of the planning and development of administrative or operational aspects of a program; AND Assisting others in analyzing problems and providing recommendations for improvement; AND Assisting others in drafting communications for management.

OR EDUCATION: You may substitute education for specialized experience as follows: Master's or equivalent graduate degree OR 2 full academic years of progressively higher graduate level education leading to a Master's or equivalent graduate degree. OR LL.B. or J.D., if related.

OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: You may qualify on a combination of education and experience. To combine education and experience, the total percentage of experience at the required grade level compared to the requirement, as well as the percentage of completed education compared to the requirement must equal at least 100 percent.

Only graduate level education in excess of the first 18 semester hours (27 quarter hours) may be combined to be considered for qualifying education. The experience may have been gained in either the public, private sector or volunteer service. One year of experience refers to full-time work; part-time work is considered on a prorated basis.

To ensure full credit for your work experience, please indicate dates of employment by month/day/year, and indicate number of hours worked per week on your resumé.

-Serve as the "alter ego" for the Director of the Intelligence Directorate of AFMC, planning, organizing, and managing the activities of the directorate. -Exercise supervisory personnel management responsibilities. -Represent the AFMC Intelligence Directorate with a variety of installation and functional area organizations. -Represent the MAJCOM in Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS) workforce boards and studies.
Ideal Candidate: The ideal candidate for this position is a seasoned leader with mastery-level knowledge of the full spectrum of intelligence operations, functions, and policies.

This individual will possess expert-level proficiency in personnel management, including EEO and security regulations, coupled with a comprehensive ability to plan, direct, and mentor a diverse staff through subordinate supervisors.

We are seeking a superb strategist who can analyze and adjust work operations to meet objectives within available resources.

The perfect candidate will have masterful communication skills, both oral and written, enabling them to resolve complex problems, author concise intelligence products, and deliver compelling presentations to senior decisionmakers.

Furthermore, the candidate must demonstrate a mastery-level ability to manage classified materials, rapidly analyze disparate information to make sound and timely recommendations under pressure, and effectively justify their assessments based on mature judgment and extensive experience.

In order to qualify, you must meet the quality experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions.

EXPERIENCE REQUIRED: Your resume must reflect the quality level of experience which demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for successful job performance required for this position.

Examples of creditable experience include: Quality experience includes a mastery level of command intelligence functions, operations, and policies with expert knowledge of personnel management, Equal Employment Opportunity policies, and safety regulations to effectively mentor and lead a team through subordinate supervisors.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1.

Mastery knowledge of a comprehensive range of intelligence functions, operations, policies, procedures, and practices and the concepts, theories, and practices of the specialist work performed in the subordinate organizations. 2.

Expert knowledge of personnel management, Equal Employment Opporunity, and safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. 3. Comprehensive ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and mentor, motivate, and appraise the staff of an organization through subordinate supervisors. 4.

Superb ability in analyzing, planning, and adjusting work operations of one or more organizational segments to meet program requirements and objectives within available resources. 5.

Mastery skill in communicating effectively with others, both orally and in writing, in working out solutions to problems or questions related to the work, writing clear and concise intelligence products, and delivering written and/or verbal presentations to senior level audiences for decision-making purposes.

PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week.

VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Additional Information: Position is designated special-sensitive and requires eligibility for access to Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI), other intelligence-related Special Sensitive information, or involvement in Top Secret Special Access Programs (SAP) to fully perform the duties and responsibilities of the position.

A non-disclosure agreement must be signed. This position has been designated by the Air Force as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Testing Program. Employee must pass initial and periodic short notice drug testing.

Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive positions presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety.

The duties of this position meets all requirements as a category 4 designation and shall not be vacated during a national emergency or mobilization without seriously impairing the capability of the parent Federal Agency or office to function effectively.

This position must be removed from the Ready Reserve and CAN NOT become a member of the Ready Reserve. (IAW: DoDD 1200.7, "Screening the Ready Reserve,").

Incumbent is subject to work other than normal duty hours, which may change daily due to operational requirements, is subject to after duty hours recall based on operational situations, may be required to carry a phone, or radio, during on and off duty time, and must be prepared to travel on short notice.

Position requires occasional temporary duty travel (CONUS and OCONUS), utilizing any or all modes of commercial and military transportation. Requires possessing and maintaining valid State Driver's License to enable operation of government and privately-owned vehicles.

Job Summary : The Content Review Operations Coordinator is responsible for managing and executing the end-to-end medical, legal, and regulatory review processes for promotional or medical content within Genentech.

This role ensures that content moves efficiently, compliantly, and transparently through the review cycle, supporting timely approvals and audit readiness. The role is critical to ensuring compliance with internal policies and external regulatory requirements while enabling speed to market for high-quality, approved content.

Develop and execute Content Review Operations plans aligned with compliance and product standards, including planning inputs and resource allocation to optimize review processes.
Lead and manage content review processes, including Medical, Legal, and Regulatory (MLR), ensuring adherence to SOPs, quality standards, regulatory requirements, and Genentech policies.
Manage material flow through review, including submission validation, agenda preparation, review meeting facilitation, follow-ups, timely decision-making, and issue resolution.
Validate and steward content metadata and business rules to support modular content product standards and align with campaign or above-campaign business needs; provide resources and ongoing support on evolving content systems, processes, and standards.
Identify and mitigate process gaps, risks, and compliance issues; escalate as needed, partner with content owners to ensure standards are followed, maintain audit trails and compliance documentation, and support experimentation to improve efficiency and operational outcomes.

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, with 5 years in roles partnering with a variety of stakeholders and 3 years in professional roles focused on content/digital asset management, content or marketing operations, content review/approval, compliance, and/or governance.
Experience using Veeva Vault PromoMats (VVPM) or similar tools as the primary system for content/digital asset management and review/approval, plus experience with Microsoft Office tools such as Excel, Teams, Word, SharePoint, and others.
Experience in healthcare, pharmaceutical, biotech, or other highly regulated industries, with a strong understanding of marketing and medical content lifecycles, digital content strategies, and regulatory compliance in marketing.
Proven ability to develop operational processes and leverage technology to improve efficiency and compliance, supported by excellent program management and advanced communication skills for collaboration with enterprise stakeholders across functions.
Additional desired experience includes knowledge of creative development and print/distribution systems, in-depth understanding of brand ecosystems and agency operations, and an adaptive, agile mindset with commitment to continuous process improvement.

We are seeking an experienced Manager, Contact Center Operations to lead day-to-day customer support center operations within a complex, multi-account delivery environment.
This role will lead teams of Associate Managers, analysts, and contact center professionals, with accountability for service-level performance, quality, productivity, customer experience, workforce utilization, and continuous improvement.
Working closely with Contact Center Operations leadership and cross-functional partners, you will translate business and client priorities into effective operational execution. You will help ensure teams consistently meet performance objectives while identifying opportunities to improve processes, leverage technology, and enhance the customer experience.
The ideal candidate is a hands-on operational leader who combines strong people leadership with analytical problem-solving and a continuous improvement mindset. You will play an important role in driving consistent execution, developing talent, and supporting the adoption of automation and AI-enabled solutions across the contact center.

Manage Operational Performance
Lead day-to-day contact center operations and ensure performance against SLAs, KPIs, quality standards, productivity targets, and customer experience objectives.
Monitor operational performance and use data and reporting to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
Establish clear expectations and accountability for team performance.
Conduct regular performance reviews and implement action plans to address performance gaps.
Ensure consistent execution of client requirements, operational procedures, and business priorities.
Lead and Develop Teams
Directly manage Associate Managers, analysts, and/or other contact center team members.
Coach and develop leaders to improve employee performance, engagement, and retention.
Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer focus, and continuous improvement.
Identify development opportunities and support talent and succession planning.
Recognize high performance and address performance issues in a timely and effective manner.
Drive Process Improvement
Identify opportunities to improve contact center processes, workflows, quality, and productivity.
Use root-cause analysis to identify and resolve recurring operational and customer experience issues.
Implement process improvements that increase efficiency, consistency, and service quality.
Share and adopt best practices across teams and delivery locations.
Support continuous improvement initiatives using structured methodologies and data-driven approaches.
Support Workforce and Resource Optimization
Partner with the Workforce Management Manager to align staffing and scheduling with customer demand and operational requirements.
Monitor staffing, capacity, utilization, productivity, and service-level performance.
Identify opportunities to improve resource utilization while maintaining customer and quality objectives.
Support forecasting, capacity planning, and operational planning activities.
Improve Customer Experience
Monitor customer experience metrics, quality results, feedback, and operational trends.
Identify root causes of customer issues and implement appropriate corrective actions.
Drive improvements in customer satisfaction, first-contact resolution, quality, and overall service experience.
Ensure teams understand how operational performance directly impacts the customer.
Collaborate Across Teams
Partner with Contact Center Operations leadership to execute operational priorities and account objectives.
Work closely with Workforce Management, Quality, Training, Technology, Finance, HR, and other functional teams.
Collaborate with client and internal stakeholders to resolve operational issues and improve service delivery.
Support consistency and best-practice sharing across the Americas, Canada, Costa Rica, and the Philippines .
Communicate operational performance, challenges, and improvement opportunities clearly to leadership.
Maintain Compliance & Operational Controls
Ensure teams follow client, regulatory, contractual, and internal policies and procedures.
Maintain strong quality and operational controls within the contact center.
Support audits, compliance reviews, and remediation activities as required.
Promote a culture of quality, risk awareness, and operational discipline.

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Technology, Operations, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship.
10+ years of contact center, BPO, or BPS experience, including significant people leadership experience.
5+ years of experience managing contact center operations , preferably in a BPO/BPS environment.
Demonstrated experience managing managers, team leaders, or other operational leadership roles.
Strong understanding of contact center KPIs, including SLAs, AHT, quality, productivity, customer satisfaction, and service-level performance.
Experience working in multi-channel customer support environments and with contact center technologies.
Experience working in regulated or compliance-driven environments.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and decision-making skills.
Demonstrated experience implementing process improvements and driving operational performance.

Experience supporting Financial Services or Life & Annuity insurance operations.
Experience working across multiple accounts, sites, or geographic locations.
Experience with Workforce Management and capacity planning.
Familiarity with contact center automation, AI, analytics, and digital technologies.
Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
Experience working with global delivery teams.
What Success Looks Like
Operational Excellence
Consistently meets or exceeds SLA, KPI, quality, and productivity objectives.

You won't be doing it alone. You'll partner closely with our People Operations & Programs team in New Zealand, fleet, people systems, compliance and health & safety, onboarding programs, and you'll be the local expert they depend on for anything Argentina/Uruguay.
We're creating this role because we're growing fast in a brand-new market, and this work can't wait. When a laptop doesn't get signed for or a vehicle handover slips, someone's first week is worse for it. You'll be the person who makes sure that doesn't happen.
This is a hands-on, varied role for someone early in their career or making a career pivot. We don't care whether you've done people operations before. We care that you excel at whatever you put your mind to, that might have looked like your studies, your sport, or something you built on your own time.

s.h: What Your Day Will Look Like
s.t:
You're in early because it's a new starter's first day. Their desk is ready, their laptop is provisioned, their merch is sorted. You want to be the one who meets them at the door.
It's 9:40 and a vehicle handover has gone sideways, the depot window moved. You drop what you're doing and sort it, because a Territory Manager without a truck can't work.
You're partnering with the Global Vehicle Fleet lead in New Zealand, working on building a more scalable process.
You overhear the customer team saying they haven't had a proper team moment in weeks. You make a note and do something about it on Friday.
Executives are flying in from Auckland and Boulder next month for a fortnight. You make the whole visit feel effortless.
You hit something nobody has written a process for. You solve it, then write the process, for Argentina first, then Uruguay.
You spend a day out on farm with a Territory Manager, because you can't support work you've never seen.
In short: operational people threads, fleet, office, and creating genuinely good experiences for our Argentina and Uruguay teams. You'll be the ask-me-anything for everyone here.

Someone who fills other people's cups. Introvert or extrovert genuinely doesn't matter to us — some of the best people on our team are each. What matters is that you give energy rather than take it, and that people want to follow you whatever your title says.
A mindset of unreasonable hospitality. You bring a customer-service instinct to how you treat colleagues.
Comfortable being uncomfortable. You'll do the job nobody wants to do because you can see it needs doing. High humility, no ego about the task.
Strong operationally, with proven ability to execute in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. Timing matters here — most of this work can't wait a week.
A systems thinker. You'll get fluent in our people systems fast and become the local expert others come to. You like building the process, not just working the queue.
High awareness and empathy. You read between the lines and put yourself in other people's shoes.
Excellent judgment and discretion. Thoughtful, high-integrity, trustworthy. People will tell you difficult things and you'll know what to do with them.
You don't need a People background. Our team has come from hospitality, retail, services, agency and design. Delivery and curiosity beat a linear HR CV.
You've grown wherever you've been — promoted, trusted with more, handed the hard thing. Or you've followed what you find genuinely interesting rather than climbing a ladder. Both are good signals to us.
Hungry and ambitious , with the horsepower to grow as the business does.
Fluent in Spanish and English. You'll be the bridge between the Argentine team and colleagues in New Zealand and the US.
Based in Buenos Aires and up for five days a week with the team. Our space is in Vicente López to start.
Genuinely interested in the work — land, livestock, and the people who farm it.
Where this could go
We're not hiring a coordinator forever. We're hiring the person who builds the foundation in Argentina, then helps us do it again in Uruguay and beyond. If you're good, this is one of the best seats in the company to grow from.
What this role isn't
Some of this work is physical, urgent and unglamorous. You'll sign for deliveries and stand in queues. Processes will break and you'll be the one who notices. There's no playbook yet, and for a while you'll be writing it while doing the job. If that sounds frustrating rather than exciting, this isn't the right role — and that's genuinely fine.
Our Office First Approach
Humans are wired for connection. Being office first is a core pillar of our culture because in-person connections drive your growth, learning, impact, and relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful work together.
We're office first, not office only. Working from the office is our default, but we flex when needed. We have a high-trust culture where everyone is trusted to do what's best for Halter.
Our office vibe is special, the high energy and spectacular people make work enjoyable. Your growth and impact are unlimited here, coming from solving problems, innovating, and constantly learning from each other.
Join our team
Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement.

About Halter
At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences.

Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance.

Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.
We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures .

We're after a Financial Operations Analyst to be the engine room of our day-to-day finance operations, covering customer accounts, supplier payments, and employee expenses. You'll be the go-to person the wider business turns to when they need something sorted, fast and right.
This is a cross-functional role by design. You'll work closely with Sales, Customer, People and teams right across Halter, not just Finance. If you like variety, own outcomes, and want your work to actually move the needle, this is for you.

Customers: Support accounts receivable process: invoicing, collections, and resolving billing queries quickly and professionally, protecting the customer relationship every step of the way.
Suppliers: Support our Financial Accountant on accounts payable: processing invoices, supplier onboarding, reconciling accounts, and being a reliable point of contact for our suppliers.
Employees: Manage the employee expense process: reviewing claims, reconciling corporate cards, employee reimbursements and keeping a high standard on details required without slowing the business down.
Cross-functional support: Be the first port of call for finance questions from teams across Halter: clear, fast, and helpful, every time.
Process improvement: Spot the gaps, fix the clunky stuff, and build better ways of working. We want someone who improves the system, not just runs it.
Month-end: Support close activities related to AR, AP and expenses, keeping our financial records accurate and audit-ready.

Experience in an accounts, finance operations, or accounts administration role, ideally across AP, AR or expenses. Sharp, numbers-hungry graduates who are keen to learn fast are welcome too.
Sharp attention to detail. You notice the things others miss, and you chase them down until they're resolved.
A genuine bias for action. You see a problem, you fix it. You don't wait to be told.
Comfortable operating at pace, with ambiguity, and without a playbook for everything.
Strong communication skills: confident chasing payments, questioning a number, or pushing back, whoever you're talking to.
A customer-first mindset, and pride in doing things properly, not just quickly.
Most of all: you're keen. You want to roll your sleeves up and build something exceptional, not just show up for the job title.

Real ownership from day one, with visibility across the whole business, not just Finance.
A seat on a team that's here to win, moves at max velocity, and backs each other to get there.
The chance to shape how finance operations work as Halter scales fast, across NZ, Australia and the US.
An office-first Auckland team that works hard, shares the wins, and doesn't take itself too seriously along the way.

s.h: Why our team loves working at Halter
s.t:
Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations.
Spectacular people solving hard problems. Our culture is designed for talented people to do work that changes lives. The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems.
You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our $1,000 personal growth fund.

Why Harvey
At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.
This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.
Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished.

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.
At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

We’re looking for a senior operator to own the quality bar behind Harvey’s human evaluations. As we scale globally, the volume of eval work is growing 10x, but volume only matters if the output is trusted. This role makes Human Data’s signal decision-grade: rigorous, calibrated, and reproducible enough that Product, Engineering, and AI Research act on it to ship.
As a member of our Evaluation Operations team, you’ll work alongside our Evaluation Operations Manager (who runs throughput and coordination) and partner closely with Applied Legal Researchers, Product, Engineering, and AI Research. You'll set the standard for what "good" looks like across eval data and methodology, and own the data analyses to make conclusions that teams will rely on, building the stakeholder trust that lets EPD act on the signal.

Own the quality bar for Harvey’s human evaluations: define what “good” looks like for eval methodology and data analysis, and produce decision-grade outputs for EPD
Author and maintain the evaluation guidelines, instructions, and databases that contract attorneys work from
Standardize and streamline rubric and evaluation design into repeatable templates and one documented methodology, partnering with Applied Legal Research (ALR), who supplies feature-specific legal depth
Own contract-attorney quality: onboarding, calibration training, inter-rater reliability, and the feedback loop (including benchmarks and gold references) that keeps judgment consistent across attorneys and over time
Conducting quantitative and qualitative statistical analyses, diagnosing error states, investigating root causes, and turning raw eval results into a structured, prioritized signal Product and ALR can act on
Run QA on vendor and contract-attorney deliverables against a defined bar before results inform a launch decision
Ensure the quality bar holds across jurisdictions and non-English geographies as coverage expands
Establish one standard, documented way to analyze eval results, and build lightweight operational dashboards to track rater capability and eval-program health
Support ALR in a review step that certifies an evaluation is sound before it scales to contract attorneys
Partner with ALR and Analytics to determine where human eval aligns with online signal and where it can provide expanded insights
What You Have
6+ years in product operations, research operations, evaluation/QA operations, or quality program management
A track record of owning quality inputs (guidelines, instructions, benchmarks, QA procedures) for complex, expert-driven or human-in-the-loop work
Experience onboarding, training, and calibrating a distributed pool of expert raters, annotators, or reviewers, and running the feedback loop that improves their quality over time
Enough grounding in measurement concepts (calibration, inter-rater reliability, sampling, rubric design) to independently set up and own the quality of our evaluation loop yourself
Experience with running quantitative and qualitative data analyses, interpreting and running statistical tests on evaluation data (natively or with AI tool support), and communicating conclusions to various stakeholders
A record of scaling and streamlining evaluation quality processes under shipping pressure, with a bias toward documentation and reproducibility over one-off analysis
Ability to work deeply with domain experts (e.g., ALR / lawyers) and translate nuanced judgment into repeatable, documented standards
Strong cross-functional coordination across Product, Engineering, Research, ALR, and data providers/vendors
Clear communicator who can build credibility and trust with stakeholders
Bias to action and high ownership, from writing the guideline to auditing a vendor batch line by line

Experience in legal tech or working with domain experts in regulated industries
Experience owning quality across multiple markets, languages, or jurisdictions
Built calibration, inter-rater reliability, or capability-tracking systems for annotation or evaluation pipelines
Experience transitioning evaluation work in-house or otherwise improving evaluation ROI
Familiarity with LLM-as-judge / automated evaluation used alongside human eval
Early employee at a hyper-growth startup, or experience at a world-class product or platform operations org

About Neon
Neon is a global payments and e-commerce platform designed to help game publishers earn more money and independence from app stores. We believe commerce should be open and transparent: clear decisions, actionable insights, and aligned incentives.

Founded by payments, fintech and gaming veterans, Neon focuses on product and partnership excellence: we share the playbook, co-pilot decisions, and abstract away risk and complexity for our customers. We’re replacing old-school, black-box relics with clear, modern, and developer-centric infrastructure.
As an early team member, you’ll have the opportunity to shape and scale Neon’s product and culture, making a direct impact on our growth and success. You’ll join a collaborative, diverse team from world-class companies like Apple, Affirm, Unity, and Visa, backed by renowned VC's including Thrive, a16z, Griffin Gaming, Ribbit, and Renegade. If you want to build disruptive technology, challenge the status quo, and help game creators thrive on their own terms, read on.

Neon is a gaming-focused Merchant of Record platform serving game publishers globally. We process payments across 50+ markets through multiple PSPs simultaneously, operating as the seller of record across card networks, local wallets, A2A rails, and alternative payment methods.
This role owns the operational backbone of that system: dispute and chargeback management, fraud operations, compliance monitoring, payment performance tracking, and operational support for Customer Success.

As the senior operator across these functions, the Payment Operations Manager sets operational standards, defines targets, owns PSP and partner operational relationships, and is accountable for outcomes across payments, risk, fraud, and compliance.

The role partners with the Head of Payments and the Risk, Fraud & Compliance Product Leader as a peer across all four functions.
This is a senior individual-contributor role . The Manager title reflects the seniority and ownership scope of the role and function, not direct reports at this stage.

Dispute & Chargeback Operations
Own dispute intake, evidence compilation, and resolution across all active payment processors and markets.
Define and own resolution SLAs and win-rate targets; identify systemic patterns and drive fixes with product and risk leads.
Prioritize and drive the roadmap for internal dispute tooling as operational infrastructure matures.
Fraud Operations
Own fraud operations and oversee investigations and transaction reviews in partnership with the Risk, Fraud & Compliance Product Leader.
Set monitoring and escalation standards across screening and decisioning tools; maintain case integrity and decision quality.
Track fraud loss trends across markets and game titles; surface and act on emerging attack patterns before they scale.
Payment Performance Monitoring
Own tracking of authorization rates, payment success rates, decline codes, and fraud losses across processors and markets.
Own post-launch metric reviews for new payment methods against defined performance thresholds.
Define the operational dashboard and alerting standard; ensure anomalies are caught before they become publisher-impacting incidents.
Customer Success Support
Serve as the senior operational point of contact for payment-related requests escalated by Customer Success.
Lead deep dives into publisher payment performance, dispute trends, and fraud exposure, producing structured analysis CS can use directly in publisher conversations.
Own the operational response to payment incidents: root cause investigation, timeline reconstruction, and remediation communication.
PSP & Partner Management
Own day-to-day operational relationships with PSPs and payment partners, including performance reviews, escalations, and issue resolution.
Hold partners accountable to performance and SLA commitments; drive improvement where markets or methods underperform.
Process, Tooling & Standards
Set and maintain operational standards, runbooks, and process documentation that others follow.
Prioritize automation opportunities and partner with the Head of Payments, Risk & Compliance, and engineering to translate operational gaps into product and tooling improvements.
Act as the senior escalation point for payment operations.
Key Success Metrics
Dispute win rate and resolution turnaround, owned and improved per processor.
Fraud operations outcomes: fraud loss rate, false positive rate, detection rate, and escalation accuracy.
PSR performance against target across active payment methods and markets, with defined review triggers on all methods.
Incident response and resolution time for publisher-impacting payment issues.
Reporting accuracy, on-time delivery, and operational process maturity as the function scales.
Ideal Profile
6-8+ years in payments operations, fraud ops, or fintech risk, with a track record of owning a function or leading operational initiatives, ideally at a PSP, Merchant of Record, or digital goods company.
Has run these functions end to end, not just participated in them; comfortable operating across multiple payment processors simultaneously, with direct experience of global PSPs such as Stripe, Adyen, PayPal, or Razorpay.
Experience owning PSP or partner relationships and influencing product, engineering, and Customer Success without formal authority.
Deep understanding of dispute and chargeback mechanics at the card network level (Visa/Mastercard rules), not just tool navigation.
Strong analytical capability: works across dashboards and data tools, builds structured reports, and finds signals in noisy transaction data.
Detail-oriented and self-directing; operates with significant autonomy across a broad and growing operational surface.
Business-level English proficiency required, written and verbal.

Win lighthouse customers and turn them into market momentum by making them wildly successful, telling their story locally, and using those wins to influence peer companies across Germany.
Embed Notion’s AI-era GTM model across the team, including agent-enabled customer journeys, first-agent workflow activation, AI/agent demo proficiency, and stronger “build with the customer” motions.

Create a talent destination in Germany by hiring builder-oriented leaders and ICs, raising the craft bar, and developing the next generation of AI-native GTM talent.
Drive operational excellence across forecasting, pipeline quality, territory planning, inspection cadence, performance management, and cross-functional execution.

A strategic and hands-on GTM operator who has scaled enterprise SaaS or AI businesses in Germany and knows how to build a market, not just inherit one. You combine second-line leadership with builder energy. Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together . Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.
Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. As General Manager, France, you will be the second-line leader responsible for overall revenue outcomes, regional GTM strategy, and the operating model for the French business.

You will lead through frontline managers, teams of Business Development Representatives, Solutions Consultants and Outcomes Architects as well as partner cross functionally with Professional Services, Channel Partnerships and RevOps.
This is a hands-on builder-leader role for an AI-native, country-first GTM model. You will bring Notion’s new GTM model to life in France: moving from a segment-first motion to a country-first, AI-native operating system where teams help customers diagnose problems, design agentic workflows, and build real systems with Notion AI.
This role sits on the EMEA Leadership Team and reports to the General Manager, EMEA.
This role will be based in Paris. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

Own the GTM strategy, operating rhythm, and growth plan for France, with accountability for overall regional revenue outcomes across Sales Assist and Self Serve contribution.

Create a talent destination in France by hiring builder-oriented leaders and ICs, raising the craft bar, and developing the next generation of AI-native GTM talent.
Drive operational excellence across forecasting, pipeline quality, territory planning, inspection cadence, performance management, and cross-functional execution.

We are seeking a Senior Operations Analyst to take on complex, ambiguous safety and risk problems and turn them into practical operational solutions that can scale.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for a versatile operator who is comfortable moving between queues, investigation, analysis, workflow design, hands-on execution, and cross-functional leadership. Depending on team needs, the role may focus on emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployment partnerships, or other new operational areas.
You will be expected to move quickly, work hands-on, and create structure without waiting for perfect requirements or a large support team. The work starts with the problem, not a prescribed process.

You may investigate unstructured user signals, stand up a lightweight workflow, build an AI-assisted tool, improve an existing operation, or help a new launch become operationally ready. The goal is to produce durable systems that other people can run, not simply complete a series of individual tasks.
The portfolio will change with company priorities and may span established harm areas, emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployments and partnerships, device safety, or new product launches. Some hires may focus primarily on cloud deployment operations, including launch readiness, partner coordination, safety workflows, and operational monitoring.

You will typically own a small number of high-impact problems at a time and will be expected to judge what needs to be built, what can stay lightweight, and when the work is ready to scale, transfer, or stop.
Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.
Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. Strong discretion, good judgment, and resilience are essential.
In This Role, You Will
Take ownership of ambiguous, high-priority safety and risk problems: define the problem, gather the right evidence, choose a practical path, drive execution, and close the loop.
Analyze structured and unstructured data, both quantitative and qualitative. This may include user reports, case narratives, conversations, escalations, and operational metrics to identify patterns, risks, and the highest-leverage interventions.
Build and test lightweight workflows, tools, automations, and decision aids that improve speed, quality, and consistency, then iterate based on real-world use.
Turn one-off insights and manual work into scalable operating mechanisms without adding unnecessary process or complexity.
Lead sensitive investigations, incident response, or launch-readiness work, including safety workflows, human review, escalation paths, partner coordination, and operational monitoring for product launches or cloud deployments.
Work directly with cross-functional and external partners to clarify ownership, resolve operational gaps, and turn incomplete signals into clear recommendations and decisions.
Measure whether the work is improving outcomes—such as quality, speed, coverage, operator effort, or risk reduction—and adjust quickly when it is not.
Help junior operators build judgment and independence through coaching, calibration, and reusable tools.
You Might Thrive in This Role If You
Have 8+ years of experience in trust and safety operations, investigations, incident response, product operations, technical program management, or another high-judgment, data-heavy operational field.
Have a track record as a scrappy generalist who can enter an unfamiliar problem, learn quickly, and deliver with limited structure or support.
Are highly data savvy, including the ability to make sense of messy qualitative or unstructured information and combine it with quantitative evidence.
Are technically fluent and hands-on with AI tools, dashboards, and data tooling, and can build or prototype practical solutions without waiting for a dedicated technical team.
Operate independently, make clear tradeoffs, and maintain momentum as priorities and requirements change.
Think in systems: you look beyond the immediate task and build approaches that can be repeated, measured, and operated by others.
Exercise strong judgment in sensitive situations involving user impact, policy, legal risk, technical constraints, and business priorities.
Communicate clearly and directly, especially in writing, and can drive decisions across teams without formal authority.

Experience in trust and safety, fraud, product safety, integrity, or another adversarial or high-severity risk domain.
Experience moving a new or immature workflow from early investigation into stable, scaled operations.
Experience supporting cloud platforms or deployment partnerships, enterprise products, product launches, connected devices, or other technically complex programs. Direct cloud experience is a plus, not a requirement.
Familiarity with SQL, lightweight scripting, no-code tools, workflow automation, or AI-assisted development.
Experience with vendor operations, quality programs, calibrations, or distributed operational teams.

OpenAI Consumer Devices is building the next generation of products that bring powerful AI into people’s everyday lives. Guided by OpenAI’s mission to ensure AGI benefits all of humanity, our team combines world-class researchers, engineers, designers, and operators who care deeply about creating useful, intuitive, and responsible technology.

You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside exceptional people on ambitious, zero-to-one challenges at the intersection of hardware, software, and AI. This is a chance to help define an entirely new category of products—and shape how people experience AI in the future.
The Systems Integration team is critical in this mission, turning complex hardware-software development into reliable product signals. Lab Operations is the physical backbone of that work: we build and maintain the device fleets, test environments, and hardware-in-the-loop labs that let teams test repeatably, understand failures, and ship with confidence.

As a Lab Operations Manager, Systems Integration , you will own the day-to-day operation of a large-scale consumer device test lab. This is a hands-on operations leadership role: you’ll keep device fleets, test rigs, lab infrastructure, inventory, provisioning, maintenance, and logistics running smoothly so engineers and QA technicians have reliable environments for validation and release testing.
We’re looking for someone who is highly organized, technically hands-on, comfortable with consumer electronics and lab equipment, and experienced operating complex physical test environments at scale. Because this is a new category of devices, you’ll have the opportunity to build the lab operating model early—shaping the systems, standards, and workflows that support products from prototype through launch.

Own device fleet and inventory: Manage configuration, deployment, tracking, lifecycle, and accurate asset records for a large fleet of consumer devices and test equipment; coordinate receiving, storage, checkout, shipping, transfers, spares, and secure disposal .
Operate and maintain the lab: Keep racks, benches, test rigs, cabling, power, networking, peripherals, and shared equipment reliable and organized; diagnose issues and coordinate repairs, replacements, and preventive maintenance .
Prepare devices for testing: Flash, provision, reset, configure, label, and assign devices to test environments .
Support testing and diagnostics: Partner with engineering and QA on large-scale test automation setups, failure reproduction, diagnostics collection, log capture, and environment resets .
Plan lab readiness and capacity: Track fleet health, rig availability, utilization, and upcoming test needs; identify constraints before they block testing .
Partner across teams: Work with hardware, systems, QA, reliability, IT, and infrastructure teams to keep the lab ready for development and release activities .

Proven track-record of operating or supporting a hardware, electronics, reliability, manufacturing, or QA test lab.
Hands-on experience managing fleets of consumer electronics, embedded devices, prototypes, or connected hardware.
Comfortable setting up, configuring, troubleshooting, and maintaining devices, test rigs, networking, power systems, and peripherals across USB, Wi-Fi, Ethernet, Bluetooth, power, and device connectivity.

Communicate clearly with engineers, QA teams, vendors, and technicians and are comfortable escalating issues with concise supporting information.
Enjoy improving the reliability, scalability, and efficiency of physical lab operations.
Basic CAD familiarity is a plus.

Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.
You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.
The challenge
RevOps at Wayflyer is a team of builders. We're not just looking for people who can spot what's broken and flag it, that skill matters and we have great people who do it well. We're looking for people who also have the technical range to build the fix themselves, independently, without waiting on someone else's roadmap.
We sit at the epicenter of an exceptionally fast-growing business running across multiple channels and partners, and it's our job to make sure the systems underneath that growth have the ability to scale. This role is for a builder who wants to see the impact of their work fast, ideally in seconds, while still thinking several steps ahead so today's quick fix doesn't turn into next year's technical debt. We want people who enjoy the instant feedback loop just as much as the long game.
What you'll actually do
Integrations & Technical Ownership: Build, maintain and improve the systems, internal automations and integrations that make our sales and CS teams faster and more effective, from the ground up.
AI-Native Systems: Build, deploy and continuously sharpen AI-native workflows and agents that augment how Sales, CS and the wider Revenue org work, not just automate around the edges.
Data, Analytics & Problem Solving: Use self-sourced data to diagnose what's actually broken, run root cause analysis, and build the fix yourself, then measure it against real KPIs and keep iterating.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Project Ownership: Work directly with Sales, Partnerships, Marketing and Finance to turn half-formed requirements into systems that actually solve the problem.
Revenue Data Hygiene: Own regular audits, deduplication, enrichment and the process fixes that keep our data usable across every system that touches it.
Driving Operational Excellence: Spot inefficiencies before anyone asks you to, prioritise ruthlessly, and build the automated solutions that let the function scale without adding headcount.
What this role could turn into
This function sits at the intersection of Revenue, Marketing, Finance, Data and Engineering, so you'll get exposure most people spend years angling for. People who do this well tend to move toward GTM strategy, GTM engineering, product roles, and beyond. The sky is the limit.
Who thrives here
You're an AI-native builder who thinks in scale, not one-off fixes, and gets uncomfortable when you spot a manual workaround. You're just as comfortable pairing with Engineering as you are in the room with Sales leadership, translating one for the other without losing anything in the middle.

You run towards the hardest, messiest problems, you don't wait for permission, and you don't need a fully-scoped brief before you start. You're always watching what the best GTM teams are building, and you'd rather pitch a bold idea than ship another incremental tweak.
We hire for range
3+ years in RevOps, MarOps, consulting or similar, but tenure isn't the point, trajectory is. Whatever your background, you're an AI-native builder with strong business acumen and a sharp eye for the difference between a good customer experience and a bad one.
You bring fluency in Python (or Node) and SQL, hands-on experience configuring HubSpot and its developer suite, and comfort with automation platforms like Zapier, Pipedream, n8n or UiPath.

You've likely configured CPQ, CLM, sales engagement or customer-success platforms before, and just as importantly, you've driven adoption of something you built, not just shipped it and walked away. Extra credit if you've built and deployed AI agents, integrated AI/LLM-based solutions into existing workflows, or built automated pipelines end to end.
Location and working policy
📍 Dublin or London, Hybrid
The good stuff
25 days off, plus public holidays. Private healthcare, life insurance, and pension. Equity, because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers. 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

What you'll actually do
Root-cause the recurring problems that slow us down. You'll define your own KPIs, dig into self-sourced data, and take your findings straight to Director and VP-level leadership.
Build automations that solve a whole business domain, not a single ticket. You'll work across Jira, Hubspot, Pipedream, Tines, and Scriptrunner, and you'll own them end to end: scoping, building, testing, launching.
Run cross-functional projects from definition to delivery. You'll own the relationship with teams like Underwriting, Product & Engineering, and Sales globally, and manage dependencies that sit outside your own team.
Find the inefficiencies that span two or more business units before anyone asks you to. You'll help shape the team's roadmap and support teammates as they grow.
Build the AI layer on top of our existing workflows. Using tools like Claude and Tines' AI Agent actions, you'll build them to triage and resolve tickets, speed up routing, and add an intelligence layer on top of existing workflows, extending efforts like our ticket-scoping assistant and fraud-detection agents, not just tinkering alongside them.
What this role could turn into
This function moves people fast. Recent paths from this seat include a Senior Operations Manager role owning a full domain end to end, a Product Ops or Automation Lead role going deeper on the technical build, or a cross-functional leadership role managing a small team of Ops generalists.
Who thrives here
Someone who digs in when something breaks instead of escalating and waiting. You've done your own homework before you ask for help, and when you do ask, you bring options, not just the question. You're relentless about root cause, not just the symptom in front of you. You're sharp on prioritisation.

You know the difference between busy and useful, and you can explain why you said yes, no, or not yet in a way people accept. People also just like working with you. You're generous with your time and knowledge, and people are generous back. You care about diversity, equality, and inclusion, and you say something when we can do better.
