Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy.

Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

Samsara's Core IT team builds the systems, processes, and experiences that let every team at Samsara do its best work.

As Manager, Business Operations, you'll own the budget, vendor, and hardware operations that keep the rest of Core IT running: SaaS spend and licensing, vendor management across our enterprise platforms, and the hardware and logistics program that equips every office and every new hire.

You'll lead a team, partner closely with internal stakeholders, and leverage external vendors and partners to scale impact across business operations.
This role will be eligible for remote work. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You want to impact the industries that run our world. Your work will have real-world impact: helping keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and keep workers safe on the job.
You want to build a function from the ground up. SaaS budget, vendor management, and hardware operations exist today. You'll help the team formalize scope, workflows, and outcomes
You're energized by our opportunity: the vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to grow a team. You'll manage a small but mighty team, with room and a mandate for the function to grow from there. You’ll use AI tools, vendors, and partners to help scale impact, get organized and improve operational efficiency.
You want colleagues who make you better. You'll work alongside people who support each other's work, push each other to think more rigorously, and share the credit when something goes well.

Own SaaS budget, forecasting, and license management across Core IT's enterprise platforms (Atlassian, Google Workspace, Slack, and others as we adopt them), including the app catalog, utilization tracking, the renewal calendar, and cost optimization.
Own vendor management for Core IT's SaaS and hardware contracts.
Own hardware and logistics operations across five regions: inventory forecasting, procurement, multi-region ordering, new hire equipment standards, new office buildout hardware, and the IT hardware budget.
Manage and develop direct reports, setting priorities across their combined scope and growing the team's capabilities and impact as the function's mandate expands.
Partner with Core IT's business systems analysts on requirements, process design, and systems support wherever their work touches SaaS, vendor, or hardware operations.
Build the operating rhythm for Business Operations: budget tracking, vendor scorecards, a renewal calendar, and the reporting that gives IT leadership real visibility into spend and vendor performance.
Partner with IT, Sales, and R&D leadership on the platform backlog and renewal decisions that cross team lines.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

5+ years of experience in vendor management, SaaS operations, IT business operations, or a related discipline, including experience managing enterprise software or hardware contracts end to end: negotiation, renewal, and spend tracking.
Experience managing people, or a demonstrated readiness to take on people management for the first time, with a clear point of view on how you'd set priorities and grow a small team.
Experience partnering across IT, finance, and business teams to manage budget and vendor relationships.

Experience managing hardware or IT asset operations across multiple regions.
Comfortable building process, reporting, and a team from scratch, in a function this early in its life.
Strong data management and analysis skills (Google Sheets/Excel and similar tools).
Experience with SaaS procurement and license optimization at a company of comparable size or complexity.

The Sr. Business Operations Manager is a strategic partner to the leadership of Samsara’s Global Support organization, driving operational excellence and enabling data-informed decision-making at scale. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution, supporting senior leadership with the insights, communications, and operational frameworks needed to run and grow the business effectively.
This role owns the annual operating plan and the operating cadence that measures performance against it.

On the planning side, you will own the capacity, headcount, and cost model that connects support volume, productivity, AI deflection, and staffing assumptions into a defensible operating plan — and act as the connective tissue between Support leadership, Workforce Management, and Finance.

On the business operations side, you will own the reporting and business review cadence for Customer Support, turning a wide set of operational metrics into a clear narrative about what is happening, why, and what leadership should do about it.
This is a high-autonomy role for a builder. You will take ambiguous, loosely scoped problems: a cost target, a capacity gap, an unexplained trend, and return with structured analysis, a defensible model, and a recommendation leaders can act on.

You will operate credibly with senior stakeholders across Support, Finance, and People, influence without direct authority, and use modern AI tools every day to work at a level of speed and rigor that would not otherwise be possible.

Success in this role looks like leaders making better decisions faster, with a plan and a set of numbers everyone trusts.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

Own the Customer Support business review cadence (monthly and quarterly reviews) end to end: metric definition and data validation, executive narrative and insight, and follow-through on the decisions and actions that come out of it.
Build and maintain the reporting frameworks and metric definitions leaders run the business on — productivity, cost to serve, CSAT, time to resolution, deflection — and make them self-serve so managers can answer their own questions.
Partner with Support leaders on the operating programs that turn plan into behavior, including productivity and incentive program design, capacity allocation, and operational improvement initiatives that measurably improve efficiency and customer experience.

This is a broad, hands-on role at the center of the People Team, and the first point of contact for colleagues in Boston and across the Americas. The remaining quarter supports Workplace Experience: keeping our Boston office running well and helping deliver events people actually want to come to. This role is hybrid and requires presence on-site for 3 days a week in our Boston office.
It suits someone who enjoys variety and is equally comfortable handling a sensitive ER case in the morning, cleaning up HRIS data in the afternoon, and setting up for an all-hands the next day. You will get exposure across the whole People function and the chance to contribute real deliverables from day one. Here's how you'll contribute:
People Operations
Be the first point of contact for employee queries, resolving them through our case management system or pointing people to the information they need.
Maintain our People Systems, keeping people records accurate, delivering timely data to Payroll, and meeting federal, state and legal compliance requirements.
Maintain HR documentation, including personnel files in hard copy, shared drives and the HRIS; create and distribute offer letters, agreements and employment verifications.
Own the administrative side of the employee lifecycle: offers, agreements, onboarding, changes, leaves of absence and departures.
Coordinate onboarding so new joiners have everything they need to succeed on their first day, and run Day 1 Orientation for Boston starters.
Track spend against People budgets and support purchasing, vendor set-up and invoice processing.
Partner with teams across the People organization to deliver projects, improve processes and drive efficiencies in areas such as learning and development, career growth, performance management, employer branding and communications, wellbeing and mental health, and diversity and inclusion.
Leverage AI tools to speed up routine drafting, summarizing and tracking, while maintaining strong judgement around accuracy and confidentiality.
Employee Relations and Advisory
Act as first-line advisor on employee relations matters: absence and leave, performance concerns, accommodation requests, complaints and investigations. You'll triage cases and handle straightforward ones end to end.
Own the ER case log: record every case, track it through to resolution, and keep notes and documentation to an audit-ready standard.
Prepare ER documentation such as invite letters, outcome letters and separation paperwork, and take minutes at formal meetings.
Coach line managers through everyday people conversations, escalating complex, high-risk or multi-jurisdiction cases to the People Partner.
Provide Tier 1 policy interpretation, applying US federal and Massachusetts employment law and Scandit policy consistently and fairly.
Spot patterns across cases and flag recurring themes to the People Partner so we fix causes, not just symptoms.
Support policy work, drafting and reviewing policies, keeping the handbook current, and helping roll out changes with clear guidance for managers.
Workplace Experience and Events
Keep the Boston office running smoothly: supplies, kitchen stock, non-IT equipment, shared spaces and equipment, all in line with health and safety standards.
Coordinate in-person, virtual and hybrid events, including team meetings, training sessions, workshops, hackathons, global ESG programs and all-company celebrations.
Handle event logistics, including room bookings, catering, A/V, signage, transport, parking and accessibility needs, and support day-of set-up, check-in, troubleshooting and breakdown.
Manage attendee communications: invitations, RSVPs, registration lists, reminders and post-event follow-up.
Build strong working relationships with building management, tenants and vendors, and maintain vendor lists, contracts and invoices.
Oversee swag and office and event inventory for new hires and upcoming events, including ordering, storage and distribution.
Support the Global Team Outing and other Workplace Experience projects alongside the wider team.
Who we look for
Experience in a People or HR operations, coordination or advisory role, ideally in a fast-growing tech or SaaS business.
Confidence handling first-line employee relations cases, with a working knowledge of US federal and Massachusetts employment law. Exposure to other US states or to Canada and LatAm is a plus.
Hands-on experience with an HRIS and a case management system, inputting data, maintaining records and pulling reports you can trust.
Excellent organization and attention to detail. You juggle competing priorities and deadlines without dropping the ball.
A real people person: a great listener and structured communicator who can deliver a "yes" and a "no" almost equally well.
A hands-on, can-do mindset. You're happy switching between an advisory conversation, a systems clean-up and setting up a room for an event.
Proactive ownership. You anticipate needs, communicate early and follow through reliably.
You stay calm under pressure, professional and friendly, and you understand the need for confidentiality in everything people-related.
Flexible and adaptable, willing to step outside your immediate scope to make a real impact.
Business proficiency in English; Spanish or Portuguese is a plus.
Comfortable with collaboration tools (Slack, Zoom, Google Workspace) and the usual office technology.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

s.h: BUSINESS OPERATIONS ANALYST, SUPPLY CHAIN (STARLINK AVIATION)
s.t:
One of the most ambitious missions that SpaceX has undertaken to date, Starlink is leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy the world's most advanced broadband internet system and largest satellite constellation to provide fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide, connect humanity, and fund Mars colonization.

Starlink business operations combines traditional planning and analysis with broader business decision-making and strategy, directly supporting SpaceX’s leadership. Business operations is embedded in daily operations, supporting both near-term execution and long-term planning.

Team members are expected to analyze data and provide recommendations and to lead cross-functional decision-making and implementation of the recommendations. Starlink business operations is lean and dynamic, operating with a fluid structure that favors high agency.

We expect high performers to expand their scope across the program’s most critical bottlenecks.

Own global S&OP (sales & operations planning) for Starlink Aviation to convert hardware into active, happy, paying customers
Analyze key performance indicators, especially active subscribers, network utilization, produce-to-activate latency, inventory turnover, and hardware unit economics (CAC, payback period); includes developing complex S&OP models and decision-making tools
Translate analysis into strategic insights and hardware mix strategy to accelerate hardware adoption, maximize lifetime value, and minimize working capital
Orchestrate global supply allocation and demand forecasting by synthesizing complex demand signals against dynamic capacity constraints, working directly with Engineering
Drive resource planning for specific verticals, including the execution of critical hardware ramp and sunset plans in close collaboration with Hardware & Manufacturing Engineering
Enable and accelerate go-to-market execution for products post-licensing and certification to ensure zero-latency deployment
Identify initiatives for improvement of Starlink’s operational trajectory, including developing, tracking, and executing business initiatives with SpaceX’s leadership

Bachelor's degree in engineering, mathematics, computer science, data science, physics, business, or supply chain
1+ years of experience in engineering, manufacturing, product management, operations, FP&A, consulting, banking, or entrepreneurship
1+ years of experience in Excel or programming

Evidence of exceptional ability, especially within an ambiguous environment
Quantitative dual degree in engineering field and economics or business field and/or equivalent professional experience
Demonstrated success driving tangible impact/influencing within a broader organization
Extreme sense of urgency and ownership; bias toward action and automation
Ability to read and interpret income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements
Strong proficiency in SQL and Python; ability to handle large datasets independently
Excellent analytical modeling skills (e.g., Excel, Power BI, Tableau, Looker)
Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly with senior business leaders

Must be available to work extended hours and weekends as needed
Willingness to travel to customer sites, other SpaceX locations, and events as needed

Monks is on the lookout for a Operations Coordinator to join our Content team and play a key role in how we allocate, optimize and support talent across our projects.
You’ll work across multiple creative and production disciplines, partnering with project teams and craft leads to understand what each project truly needs, identify the right talent for the work, and make smart staffing decisions across competing priorities. This is more than a scheduling or booking role.

We’re looking for someone who can understand the bigger picture, challenge requests when needed, anticipate problems, and proactively find solutions that make the best use of our teams, time and budgets.

Own resource allocation across multiple projects and disciplines, balancing availability, skills, utilization, timelines and business priorities.
Partner with Project Managers, Producers, Operations and craft leads to understand project needs and build effective staffing plans.
Assess briefs and scopes critically, challenging staffing requests when needed and recommending the right roles, allocations and timing for the work.
Navigate competing priorities and resource constraints, negotiating with stakeholders and proactively proposing viable alternatives.
Maintain accurate visibility of bookings, availability and capacity to support fast and informed staffing decisions.
Build strong relationships with talent and craft leads to understand individual strengths, experience and project fit.
Identify recurring operational challenges and proactively improve processes, workflows and ways of working.
Use data, automation and AI where relevant to improve resource planning, visibility and operational efficiency.

Strong experience in Resource Management, Creative Operations, Production Operations, Traffic Management, Workforce Planning or a similar role within an agency or fast-paced creative/production environment.
Strong understanding of creative and production workflows, with the ability to quickly understand different disciplines and translate project needs into effective staffing solutions.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple requests, resources and priorities simultaneously.
Highly autonomous and solutions-oriented: you’re comfortable making decisions, negotiating priorities and moving things forward without constant direction.
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including the confidence to constructively push back, manage expectations, clearly communicate issues and propose alternatives.
Solid scoping skills, with the ability to translate project needs into realistic timings, roles and resource estimates.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to keep resource and capacity information accurate in a fast-moving environment.
Good understanding of budgets, timelines and the cost implications of staffing decisions.
Excellent written and spoken English, with professional fluency to confidently navigate nuanced conversations, negotiations and relationships with global stakeholders.
Comfortable working with resource/project management tools such as Monday.com, Asana, Jira, Notion or similar.

Experience improving operational processes through automation, AI or data.
Project Management experience combined with a strong interest in resource planning and operations.

Monitoring of operational deadlines, required inputs, owners, and cross-functional follow-ups.

Quality control of operational data and reporting before leadership or client distribution.

You’ll be joining a team that delivers high‑quality e‑commerce data across more than 40 countries. We’re looking for a detail‑oriented, analytically minded Data Operations Analyst to be part of our dynamic, multicultural team. In this role, you’ll contribute to the entire data operations lifecycle—from validating, extracting, and processing digital transaction data to troubleshooting data quality issues and partnering with cross‑functional teams.
This is a great opportunity for early‑career professionals eager to build a solid foundation in data analysis within a client‑focused environment. You’ll also have the chance to drive new initiatives and continuous improvements.

If you enjoy solving puzzles, you’ll feel right at home: your logical thinking and analytical mindset will help you navigate complex challenges, identify patterns, and uncover insights. With constant learning at the core of this role, curiosity and ownership will be essential to your success.

Data Extraction
Build data extractors to parse e-receipts using NielsenIQ’s proprietary markup language and RegEx.
Debug and fine-tune templates to make sure they’re accurate, then validate your work with SQL and BI tools.
Keep documentation clear and communicate effectively with tech teams and client-facing teams.
Adapt extraction logic as data formats and business needs change.
Stay up to date with our internal processes and tools.
Data Quality & Analysis
Conduct comprehensive checks to ensure data is complete, accurate, consistent, and correctly parsed, leveraging BI tools and SQL.
Investigate anomalies and irregularities specific to transactional data.
Write and optimize SQL queries, and build dashboards to support large‑scale analysis.
Prepare clear, actionable reports for client‑facing teams.
Process Improvement
Spot opportunities for automation and help improve our processes and tools.
Support strategic projects aimed at improving operational workflows.
Work closely with developers, analysts and client-facing teams to design solutions together.
Keep operational and project documentation up to date.

First experience (internship, projects) in data operations, analytics or tech related roles.
Basic SQL skills: Ability to write simple queries to retrieve and inspect data; Can read and understand more complex queries written by others; Understands table structures, relationships, and how data is organized within a database.
A logical, analytical mindset to tackle complex tasks and spot patterns in data.
Great communication skills and attention to detail (crucial when working with data that people rely on to make decisions).
Fluency in English.

Hands-on experience with at least one BI tool like Tableau, Power BI, Looker etc.
Knowledge of e-commerce data and industry trends.
Familiarity with analytical platforms like Snowflake or Databricks.
Previous experience in QA or data validation.
Familiarity with HTML, XML, RegEx, or other scripting/markup languages.
Experience working in agile environments and understanding basic software development processes.
